editorial:
Imagine losing your husband and your aunt in a very short time. That is exactly what happens to Rini, and it makes her life a total nightmare. When she goes back to her hometown to mourn, things get even scarier because her young son, Hafis, vanishes and is found passed out in the woods. You can really feel her panic as she tries to protect the only family she has left. The movie has a heavy, spooky vibe from the start, and it uses the idea of a ghost following you during prayer to make you feel uneasy every time a character bows down.

What really works here are the jump scares and the tension. The acting is solid, and the pacing keeps you on edge without feeling too slow. One downside is that some of the scares feel a bit repetitive, but the emotional bond between mother and son keeps you invested. If you enjoy supernatural thrillers that play with your faith, you should definitely give this a go. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the dark details, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like owning your movies.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the ghost is trying to take Hafis to the other side. Rini has to fight her own fear and doubt to save her son. She eventually realizes that strong faith and prayer are the only ways to stop the entity. After a scary showdown, she manages to break the ghost's hold on her child. The movie ends with the family safe, though the trauma leaves a lasting mark on them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural ghosts and religious horror stories.
